name: Integrated Appositive Name
pattern: Nom[descriptive noun + proper-name expression identifying the referent]

entry.name: Integrated Appositive Name
entry.pattern: Nom[descriptive noun + proper-name expression identifying the referent]

1.definition: Identifies the bearer of a nominal description by appending a name without a supplementary break.

projection.target: Both parts concern the same river. A name replacement changes the referent identified. An ordinary modifier like river water gives no comparable identification.
projection.evidence: See the cited discussion and the constructed illustration.

curious.title: A name added right after a description
curious.summary: A name can follow a descriptive noun with no pause, so the two together pick out one particular thing.
curious.body: In The river Wye flooded, river describes the thing and Wye names it. There's no comma or break between them, so the two sit together as one unit. Both parts are about the same river. Swapping the name changes which river you mean. That's what makes this different from an ordinary describing word: river water, for example, doesn't name the particular river in the same way. This dictionary marks the analysis as provisional.
curious.try: Think of a description plus a name, such as a kind of place followed by its name. Does the name still pick out one particular place?

teacher.summary: Helps explain a name attached to a descriptive noun without a supplementary break.
teacher.explain: The pattern is a Nom made of a descriptive noun plus a proper-name expression that identifies the referent: the river Wye. Because there's no supplementary break, the name is integrated into the phrase. Both parts concern the same river, and replacing the name changes the referent identified. An ordinary modifier, such as river in river water, gives no comparable identification. This dictionary treats the pattern as a specialization of the Nom, and marks the analysis as provisional.
teacher.terms: Traditional grammar sometimes calls this restrictive apposition. In this dictionary: integrated appositive name.

contrasts.note: River is an ordinary modifier of water and names no particular river.

watch_for: A learner might treat Wye in the river Wye as an ordinary describing word, like river in river water.

cite: Reynolds, Brett, ed. 2026. "Integrated Appositive Name." English Constructionary. https://brettreynolds.ca/constructionary/linguist/restrictive-appositive-name-001/ (snapshot 2026-11-19, ef810bb).
